column1: # TEST-GLOBALS — process-globals that two tests of one binary reach, or that a test writes, each
# with the class that makes it safe (T-TEST-PROCESS-GLOBALS, 2026-10-24).
# crates/bt-source/tests/test_globals.rs holds this list equal to the tree both ways: a global its
# grammar finds and no row names is red, and a row that is no longer one is red. A row is keyed by
# file, global (its module path and name; a body-declared one by its body's path) and binary (the
# target whose tests share it: each target has a copy of its own).
# Classes the guard checks itself: lock:<NAME> (every test that reaches the global also reaches
# the unit lock NAME), single writer (exactly one test's reach writes it), one main (the binary
# runs without the harness), run=alone / run=serial (every test that reaches it carries that run
# condition on scripts/ci/ignored-tests.txt). Classes by hand: per-test key, monotone, write-once
# (its writes are held to once-writes by the guard), not on a test thread, serial helpers.
# scripts/ci/check-test-globals.ps1 admits an added row of a checked class with its dated reason,
# and an added row of a by-hand class only under a new "# widened <date> by <ticket> (+n rows)"
# line, in a change to the scan. A reason is "YYYY-MM-DD: why".
